name: Healthcare PHI Policy Pack
description: PHI / HIPAA DLP build, predefined-first, six-engine architecture (from the customer's build document) plus the Fed pack's US PII and US PHI coverage. Seven custom dictionaries cover the HIPAA identifiers no predefined dictionary does (MRN, DOB, health-plan member id incl. Medicare MBI, address/ZIP) plus clinical-narrative structure, insurance/billing vocabulary and elevated-protection condition markers (SUD, mental health, HIV, genetic, reproductive); twelve more (HC- prefixed, from the Fed pack) give high-confidence and 500-byte-proximity variants of SSN, TIN and driver's licence clones and of alien registration, date of birth and US passport; everything else comes from Zscaler's predefined dictionaries (Names (US), SSN, NPI, driver's licences, TIN, Medical Information, Diseases, Drugs, Treatments, NDC, Medical Document, Medical Imaging, Insurance Document, Self-Harm & Cyberbullying, Illegal Drugs, Credit Cards). Ten engines: HIPAA Critical (three pathways), Narrative / Low Volume, Identity Trifecta, Sensitive Subcategory, Pharmacy / Claims / Billing, Bulk PHI as a Sum of identifier matches in three tiers (> 1, > 50, > 500) behind three rules, US PII (identity data with no clinical context), US PHI at medium and high confidence (a second, independent PHI opinion) and Financial Information (payment cards, routing numbers and tax forms: the PCI DSS scope beside HIPAA, with nine more HC- dictionaries from the Fed pack). Twelve inline rules, each mirrored one-for-one onto Endpoint DLP, SaaS Security API and Outbound Email DLP. Every rule ships DISABLED, monitor-only, at INFO severity. See PHI_HIPAA_BUILD.md for the regulatory decision path, the 18-identifier coverage map, tiers and tuning notes. Containment is outside this pack.
references: Customer build document: PHI / HIPAA DLP Build — Predefined-First Dictionary and Engine Reference for Zscaler ZIA (6-Engine Architecture)
HIPAA Privacy Rule 45 CFR 164.514(b)(2)(i) (18 identifiers); Breach Notification Rule 45 CFR 164.400-414; 42 CFR Part 2 (Feb 16, 2026 alignment); GINA
Zscaler: About DLP Engines (All / Any / Sum operators, nesting limits)
notes: Engine 6 uses the Engine Builder's Sum operator, written in the API's expression form ((D1.S + D2.S + …) > n): the identifier matches are totalled across the seven dictionaries. The design's one engine with rule-level match-count conditions becomes three engines (> 1, > 50, > 500) behind three rules, because a ZIA DLP rule has no match-count condition of its own.

Predefined dictionaries are referenced by their portal display names; the deploy resolves them by API code, display name or description, and a name this tenant does not expose is pruned from the engine with a warning. Tenants created before April 4, 2025 may need Zscaler Support to enable the medical dictionary bundle (Medical Imaging, Insurance Document, NDC, Treatments).
Proximity is bytes across the extracted text stream: 50 for MRN, DOB, member id and address; the sensitive-condition markers match on any phrase or gene pattern instead.
Custom-Address-ZIP is not wired into an engine by default (ZIP alone is very noisy); add it to the claims pathway only where ZIP appears beside billing context.

Rules ship without file_types and with OCR on. The three Bulk rules should be ordered Major, Significant, Small once enabled so a transaction lands in exactly one tier under Rule Order; under Evaluate All Rules the Block on Major or Significant wins anyway.

Every rule ships DISABLED and monitor-only (ALLOW, or report incident on SaaS). Nothing in the pack blocks; enforcing a rule is the customer's decision in the portal once incidents have been reviewed, and the journey records it as progress.

Engines 7-9 and the twelve HC- dictionaries are the Fed pack's US PII and US PHI build, renamed so the two packs can share a tenant. The clones (SSN, TIN, driver's licence) resolve their template per tenant; a tenant that does not expose one has the clone skipped and the engine created without that term, named in the plan.

Engine 10, HIPAA Financial Information, comes from the Fed pack's Financial Information engine (HC- prefixed copies): payment cards and magnetic tracks, ABA routing numbers, W-2 / 1099 / K-1 / 1040 forms and Zscaler's financial classifiers, the PCI DSS scope a provider or payer carries on claims, billing and payroll.
audience: Covered entities, business associates and their vendors under HIPAA: providers, payers, pharmacies, clearing houses.
when_to_use: The customer needs PHI detection that maps to the HIPAA identifiers and to breach-reporting tiers, with elevated handling for 42 CFR Part 2, GINA and state-protected categories. Start every rule in monitor mode; enable Engine 1 first, then 2, 3 and 5, then 4 and the Bulk tiers (the build document's phases).
